entries.content: Decades ago the Bloom, a viral agent that rewrites living tissue, turned populations, animals and whole ecosystems into biological monsters. States collapsed; corporations did not. They now own cities, laws and armies. Their soldiers are bio-cybernetic constructs: grown, augmented, flashed with combat firmware, and owned as assets.

Every off-spec unit carries a corporate override implant. The commander cannot trigger it himself; he can only file a request to his corporation's oversight office, which approves a limited number per week. Compel: a neural compliance burst, the unit executes one order and remembers being forced. Suppress: full motor lockdown for minutes, stops a desertion or an attack in progress. Terminate: permanent deactivation, approved only with cause, irreversible. Units know exactly who filed the request.

The Correctional Command Program (CCP) is where off-spec units are dumped: penal units sent where losses do not matter. Command goes to people who also do not matter: convicted officers, offered a sentence reduction for every mission survived. "The scrap leads the scrap" is the joke every corporate clerk makes about the CCP. The player is the punchline.

The Bloom is a viral agent that rewrites living tissue. It turned populations, animals and whole ecosystems into biological monsters and collapsed the old states. Corporations treat it as a hazard, a resource, or both.

Not every unit leaves the vat to spec. Off-spec units carry a malfunction in mind, body, implants or viral suppression. They are too expensive to scrap and too unreliable for regular service, so they are dumped into the Correctional Command Program.
The base is a decommissioned CCP Outpost assigned to the unit. Places: commander quarters, unit quarters, mess hall, training yard, workshop, medbay, roof, garage, comms room, perimeter.
Vesper Somatics is a biotech corporation: it grows soldiers and treats the Bloom as a resource. Clean labs, filthy ethics.
Kestrel-Ward Industrial is a heavy industry and cybernetics corporation: more metal than flesh, brutal efficiency, quotas.
Aurum Concord is a finance and logistics corporation. It owns the debt of everyone else.
Sable Line is a security contractor: the corporation other corporations hire to clean up.
District 7 Quarantine: an overgrown arcology with fungal Bloom growth. Typical enemies: human mutants, beast mutants.
The Ashway: a dead highway lined with scavenger camps. Typical enemies: marauders, beast mutants.
Corridor K-12: mining tunnels and machinery. Typical enemies: human mutants, enemy soldiers.
Drowned Market: a flooded commercial district. Typical enemies: marauders, human mutants, rare anomalies.
The Garden: the Bloom epicenter, with wrong geometry. Typical enemies: anomalies, hostile off-spec units.
Bio-mutants (human): common. They inflict Infect and attack in swarms.
Bio-mutants (beast): common. Fast, they cause bleeding and use pack tactics.
Marauders: common. They use human tactics, carry loot and fight from cover.
Enemy corporate soldiers: rare. Disciplined and armored, they follow orders of their own.
Hostile off-spec units: rare. They have defects themselves, a mirror of the squad.
Anomalies: very rare. They deal stress directly and break rules (row-ignoring, delayed effects).
